title: A default compare on several series always runs XGBRegressor, which no install of skforecast-ai provides, so it always fails; a missing foundation backend is instead left out with a notice

primary.title: A default compare on several series always runs XGBRegressor, which no install of skforecast-ai provides, so it always fails; a missing foundation backend is instead left out with a notice
primary.input: Dataset data/multi_wide.csv (3 monthly series, 96 rows). Calls: profile {data_path, target:[store_a,store_b,store_c]} -> plan {steps:12} -> create_cv {plan_id} -> compare {cv_id} (no candidates). Environment: plain install, xgboost not importable (pyproject declares xgboost in no dependency or extra).
primary.observed: profile summary: "Alternative estimators: ['XGBRegressor', 'Ridge']". create_cv cost.compare_estimator_fits=3, which counts the XGB candidate. compare leaderboard row 3: 'ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries+XGBRegressor', error "ValueError: XGBRegressor needs the 'xgboost' package, which is not installed (pip install xgboost)." The summary says "1 configuration failed to run and is ranked last". The same response has a MissingBackendWarning notice: "ForecasterFoundation left out: its default model ... needs the 'chronos-forecasting' package". So one missing package means 'left out with a notice' and the other means 'failed candidate'.
primary.expected: Missing packages handled the same way: the default candidate set leaves out an estimator whose package is not installed (with the same kind of notice as for ForecasterFoundation), or the profile does not propose an estimator that cannot run where the server runs.
primary.agent_impact: Every default multi-series comparison in a standard install reports a failed configuration. An agent following the skill ('A candidate of compare that fails ... get_failure(comparison_id, candidate) says why') spends a call on a traceback, then tells the user something failed and advises installing xgboost, which the user never asked for. The cost from create_cv also counts a candidate that never trains. tests/tests_mcp/test_tool_compare.py::test_tool_compare_default_candidates_of_the_profile sees this and accepts it ('A candidate whose library is not installed (XGBoost) fails, as it may'), so the suite treats it as acceptable rather than catching it.
primary.skill_reference: SKILL.md step 6: 'Without `candidates` it runs the forecasters the profile recommends for the family of the data ... or the estimators of the recommended forecaster when that leaves one'. Errors: 'A candidate of `compare` that fails is ranked last instead of failing the call: `get_failure(comparison_id, candidate)` says why.'

title: Thousands separators in a ';' file are silently read as decimal marks ('1.020' read as 1.02)

primary.title: Thousands separators in a ';' file are silently read as decimal marks ('1.020' read as 1.02)
primary.input: profile {"data_path": "<data>/thousands_dot_mixed.csv", "target": "y"}. The file is a ';' export of amounts between 870 and 2050, with values below 1000 written plain and the rest with '.' as thousands separator: 2015-01-01;870 / 2015-03-01;987 / 2015-04-01;1.020 / 2015-05-01;1.234. It is 60 monthly rows. The flow then calls plan(steps=6) and forecast.
primary.observed: profile succeeds: 'Target statistics: min 1.01, max 990, mean 396.8, std 472.7', notices []. forecast succeeds: 'pred: min=-2.8476, max=979.85', notices []. No error or notice anywhere says that the decimal mark was guessed or that the column mixes magnitudes of 1 and 1000. A quoted "1,020" in a ';' file (thousands_comma_mixed_semi.csv) gives the same statistics silently.
primary.expected: Read '1.020' as 1020, or stop with data_unreadable ('decimal mark cannot be told'), as the server already does for '1,841' in a tab file. At the least, a DataProfileWarning should say that values such as '1.020' were read as decimals and the column mixes magnitudes.
primary.agent_impact: The agent follows the SKILL ('profile detects both ... pass sep and decimal only when an error says they cannot be told'), gets no error and no notice, and reports a forecast and accuracy built on a target that is wrong by a factor of 1000 in half of its rows. Nothing in the response tells it to check. This is the silent mis-parse the axis was meant to exclude, on a very common European Excel export.
primary.skill_reference: SKILL.md Inputs: "Files: ... separated by `,`, `;` or tabulators, with `.` or `,` as decimal mark. `profile` detects both and the profile records them; pass `sep` and `decimal` only when an error says they cannot be told." Tests in tests/tests_profiling/test_detect_csv_dialect.py cover ',' thousands but not '.' thousands in a ';' file.

create_cv for the Ridge plan has two notices:
- MissingValuesNotice: "Without touching the data, an estimator that accepts missing values (such as 'LGBMRegressor', with `refine_plan` and a new `create_cv`) lets `backtest` run on every fold".
- UserWarning: "...choose an estimator that accepts missing values (for example 'LGBMRegressor') to backtest every fold."

create_cv for the LGBMRegressor plan has notices: [] (none).

backtest then fails: {"code":"invalid_argument","message":"The target has 1 missing value(s) in the test folds (2017-07-01 00:00:00), counting the missing timestamps that asfreq() restores. skforecast cannot compute the metrics on them, whatever the estimator.
